memory_verse: "He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit." —Romans 8:11, NASB
sermon_title: A Freedom Only Christ Can Give

days.focus: External vs. Internal: The Certificate That Doesn't Count
days.message_reflection: The sermon described an 'external life certificate' — a good reputation before others — and then immediately said it is 'fit for nothing' when we stand before God. Thinking honestly about your own life this past week, what specific attitudes, thoughts, or motives were on the inside of your cup that your external certificate did not show?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:11 says the same Spirit who raised a dead body from a tomb is the one living inside you right now. Zac Poonen often pressed believers to ask whether they are actually experiencing the Spirit's power in daily life or simply holding it as a doctrine. What specific attitude — resentment, self-pity, a craving you return to — has remained unchanged in you for weeks or months, and have you genuinely believed that the resurrection power described in this verse is meant to touch that exact thing, today, in your ordinary circumstances?

days.focus: What God Actually Sees: The Heart God Judges
days.message_reflection: The sermon quoted 1 Samuel 16:7 — 'The Lord looks at the heart' — and applied it to the coming day of judgment, saying God will be looking at our secret thoughts, motives, and attitudes rather than our public testimony. What is one thing that God sees in your heart right now that you have been hoping others will not notice, and are you more concerned that people might find out, or that God already knows?
days.verse_reflection: John 6:63 says 'It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing,' and Romans 8:11 anchors that life-giving Spirit in the same power that raised Jesus bodily from the dead. Zac Poonen consistently warned that many believers rely on their own willpower and spiritual disciplines while the Spirit's actual life-giving work remains theoretical to them. Is there a specific area of inner deadness — a cold attitude toward someone, a persistent impurity of motive — where you have been trying harder rather than genuinely depending on the Spirit who indwells you to bring resurrection life to that exact place?

days.focus: What Jesus Came to Proclaim: Release to the Captives
days.message_reflection: The sermon described Jesus deliberately searching for Luke 4:18 as the text for his very first sermon, and said this reveals the deepest burden of God's heart — to proclaim release to those captive to inward sin, not just to help people maintain good outward behavior. According to what the sermon said, what kind of people was Jesus specifically addressing when he read that passage in the synagogue, and does that description fit you on any day between Monday and Saturday?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:2 speaks of 'the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus' setting us free from 'the law of sin and death,' and Romans 8:11 grounds that freedom in the Spirit of the One who raised Jesus dwelling in mortal bodies. Zac Poonen has drawn a sharp line between forgiveness of sin — which many Christians gratefully receive — and actual freedom from sin's power in daily life, which far fewer seem to experience. When you read 'freed from the law of sin and death,' does that describe your actual experience from Monday through Saturday, or is it still mainly a statement you believe about the past rather than a reality you are walking in today?

days.focus: The Hospital, Not Just the Family: Honesty About Being Sick
days.message_reflection: The sermon said the church is not only a family but also a hospital, and that Jesus came not for the externally righteous but for those willing to say 'everything is not okay' — to tip the cup over and show God what is inside. The sermon asked whether you are happy with a good external testimony while privately knowing your Monday-to-Saturday life looks very different. Are you currently living more like someone maintaining appearances or like someone who has walked into the hospital and said honestly, 'I am sick and I need help'?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:5-6 says those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, while those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit — and the mind set on the flesh is death. Romans 8:11 then says the same Spirit who gives that mindset actually dwells in your mortal body. Zac Poonen often challenged believers to examine not just their actions but the direction their mind drifts when no one is giving them external accountability. What do your thoughts naturally move toward when you are alone, bored, or hurt — and does the pattern of where your mind actually goes reflect someone in whom the Spirit of life is ruling, or someone still largely governed by the flesh?

days.focus: Do You Wish to Be Well? The Question Jesus Still Asks
days.message_reflection: The sermon spent significant time on the man at the pool of Bethesda who had been ill for 38 years and kept trying to help himself, and said Jesus's question — 'Do you wish to be well?' — is the same question being asked of every person in the room. The sermon also acknowledged that some people have tried for so long that they have quietly settled and given up. Have you settled into a particular sin, anxiety, bitterness, or bondage the way this man had settled beside the pool — still going through motions but no longer truly expecting to be made well?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:9-11 moves from 'the Spirit of God dwells in you' to 'He who raised Christ from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit who dwells in you' — the sequence is indwelling first, then actual life imparted to the body. Zac Poonen has repeatedly pointed out that many believers know the Spirit lives in them as a positional truth but have never surrendered a specific area of their mortal body — their tongue, their eyes, their habits — to that Spirit's actual governing power. What is one concrete habit or physical appetite in your daily life that you have never specifically, consciously offered to the Spirit described in Romans 8:11, trusting Him to give life there rather than managing it by self-effort?

days.focus: Freed from What the Law Could Not Free: The Freedom Only Christ Gives
days.message_reflection: The sermon opened and closed with Acts 13:39 — that through Jesus, everyone who believes is freed from all things from which the Law of Moses could not free them — and explained that the Law can produce a good external testimony but cannot clean the inside of the cup. As you look back over this week's reflection, what is one specific inward thing — a thought pattern, a motive, an attitude — that you have been trying to manage through self-discipline or external accountability rather than receiving the freedom that Acts 13:39 says Jesus actually provides?
days.verse_reflection: Galatians 2:20 says 'it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me,' and Romans 8:11 says the Spirit of the One who raised Jesus dwells in your mortal body — both verses locate the source of transformed life inside the believer, not in external rules or effort. Zac Poonen has consistently taught that the deepest issue in the Christian life is not the sins we commit but the self-life we protect: the 'I' that wants credit, comfort, and control even while performing religious duties. As you memorize 'He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit,' ask yourself honestly: is there a version of yourself — your reputation, your self-image, your sense of being a spiritually serious person — that you are preserving and that the Spirit is being quietly asked not to touch?
